entries.m: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. A screening index of relative weight — not a measure of body composition, adiposity, or individual health.
Square root of (height in cm × weight in kg ÷ 3600). The most widely used BSA estimate for drug dosing and physiological indexing.
Devine ideal body weight with adjusted body weight for obesity. Used where lean mass governs dosing (e.g. aminoglycosides, tidal volume).
Circumference at the midpoint of the left upper arm. A standalone admission criterion for acute malnutrition in children 6–59 months, independent of weight-for-height.
Estimates creatinine clearance from age, weight, sex and serum creatinine. Still the reference equation for many drug-dosing licences even where eGFR is reported.
Sodium minus chloride minus bicarbonate, corrected for albumin. Separates high-anion-gap from normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
Calculated osmolality (2Na + glucose + urea) versus measured. Effective osmolality omits urea and is the value used in HHS criteria.
Hyperglycaemia draws water into the extracellular space and dilutes measured sodium. Correction reveals the true sodium and therefore the true water deficit.
Adjusts total calcium for albumin binding. Ionised calcium remains the definitive measurement where available.
Compares sodium and creatinine handling in urine and plasma. Helps separate pre-renal from intrinsic (tubular) causes of acute kidney injury.
Pure arithmetic conversion between an ordered rate in mL per hour and a gravity-set drop rate. This artifact converts; it does not decide what fluid or what rate a patient should receive.
Weight-based maintenance water requirement. Maintenance is not resuscitation and not deficit replacement — the three are calculated and prescribed separately.

Acute glucocorticoid deficiency causing hypotension unresponsive to fluid. Hydrocortisone is given on clinical suspicion; confirmation follows treatment.
A seizure lasting 5 minutes or more, or recurrent seizures without recovery between them. Treatment is time-driven, and the commonest failure is under-dosing the benzodiazepine.

Eight clinical and laboratory features supporting a diagnosis of acute appendicitis. It stratifies probability; it does not decide the operation.
Mechanical blockage of bowel. The core questions: small or large bowel, complete or partial, and is the bowel strangulated?
Perforation of a Peyer's patch ulcer in the terminal ileum during enteric fever. A major cause of peritonitis in endemic regions with high death rate if surgery is delayed.
A protrusion of a viscus or part of a viscus through a defect in the wall that normally contains it. Classified by site and by clinical state.
A prioritised sequence that finds and treats what kills first. Each step is completed and any problem treated before moving on.

entries.t: FEAST (2011) — Fluid bolus in African children

entries.m: Does early objective detection of postpartum bleeding plus an immediate treatment bundle reduce severe outcomes? Measuring blood loss with a calibrated drape and then delivering a fixed bundle immediately is dramatically better than eyeballing loss and treating stepwise.

Does an enhanced prevention package reduce death in people starting ART with advanced HIV? People presenting with advanced HIV need a prevention package, not just ART.

a: transfusion in african children with severe anaemia

entries.m: How does dolutegravir with tenofovir alafenamide compare with efavirenz-based first-line ART? Dolutegravir is more effective as first-line ART but carries a metabolic and weight-gain signal that needs monitoring.
Can children with non-severe drug-susceptible TB be treated for 4 months instead of 6? Shortening treatment to 4 months is safe for children with non-severe drug-susceptible TB.
Is a single dose of HPV vaccine effective against persistent HPV infection? One dose of HPV vaccine may be enough for protection against the oncogenic types that matter most.
Should kangaroo mother care start immediately after birth rather than after stabilisation? Starting skin-to-skin care immediately, before stabilisation, saves the lives of low-birth-weight infants.

entries.m: Is the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine efficacious in African children? A second malaria vaccine with strong efficacy and a manufacturing profile suited to mass supply.

entries.m: Does tranexamic acid reduce death in bleeding trauma patients? Early tranexamic acid saves lives in bleeding trauma.
